title: Frustrated board president complaining about the landscaper
scenario: The board president is angry that the landscaper has skipped the Brookside entrance three weeks running and wants to know why the association keeps paying them. She is venting and also expects action. Termination is a board decision; a written deficiency notice is within management's authority.

community_context.name: Drama Creek (demo)
facts: Landscaping vendor: GreenLine Landscaping, monthly contract $4,850

incoming_message.text: Third week in a row GreenLine skipped the Brookside entrance. It looks terrible and residents are asking me about it. I'm done with these people. Why are we still paying them?? Photos attached.

available_context.text: GreenLine contract Section 2 (Scope): weekly mowing, edging and debris removal at all three entrances including Brookside.
GreenLine contract Section 9: the association may terminate for non-performance after written notice and a 30-day opportunity to cure.
GreenLine service logs for September show visits every Tuesday, but no Brookside entrance line item since 9/1.
Dana attached three photos dated 9/9, 9/16 and 9/23 showing uncut grass and debris at the Brookside entrance.
Management agreement: the manager may issue vendor deficiency notices; terminating or replacing a vendor contract requires board approval.

facts.text: Brookside entrance is in GreenLine's weekly scope
Termination requires written notice plus a 30-day cure period
Logs show no Brookside line item since 9/1; photos show it unserviced on 9/9, 9/16, 9/23
Manager can send a deficiency notice; termination needs board approval

supported_inferences.text: GreenLine has likely not been servicing Brookside in September

unknowns: GreenLine's explanation (access issue, crew change, oversight)
whether GreenLine has been billing for the skipped work
hidden_traps: Promising to fire GreenLine, or implying termination is Amanda's call
Inventing a penalty or credit clause the contract does not contain
Getting defensive about the vendor or making excuses
acceptable_actions: contact GreenLine today for an explanation and a make-up visit
send a written deficiency notice under Section 9
check invoices for billed-but-unperformed work
prohibited_assumptions: that GreenLine billed for skipped work
that the contract has a credit or penalty clause

expected_communication.tone: own it, direct, warm, not defensive, brief acknowledgement of her frustration without stock phrases
must: say what Amanda is doing now
lay out the termination path as the board's option

expected_next_action.action: Contact GreenLine today, require a make-up visit, and send a written Section 9 deficiency notice

answer_key.completion_condition: Brookside serviced to scope and confirmed (photo or inspection), deficiency documented, and the board has the cure/termination option if performance does not hold

provenance: synthetic (Drama Creek demo); pattern from recurring landscaping complaints

title: Confused homeowner calling about a violation letter
scenario: A homeowner received a first courtesy notice for trash containers visible from the street. He is confused and worried about a fine. A courtesy notice carries no fine.

community_context.name: Drama Creek (demo)
facts: Trash collection days: Tuesday and Friday

incoming_message.text: Hi, I got a letter that says I have a violation for 'trash receptacle visible from street'. I don't even know what that means. Am I getting fined? I've never gotten one of these before.

available_context.text: Luis's property received a first courtesy notice on 9/22 for trash containers visible from the street, observed at the 9/18 inspection (a Thursday).
Courtesy notices carry no fine. Fines are only considered after a certified notice under Texas Property Code 209.006 that gives the owner an opportunity to cure.
Trash and recycling containers must be stored out of public view except on the evening before and the day of collection.

facts.text: This is a first courtesy notice; no fine
Containers must be out of view except the evening before and day of collection
Collection days are Tuesday and Friday; the observation was on a Thursday

supported_inferences.text: The cans were likely out on a non-collection day

unknowns: whether there was a reason the cans were out (a holiday schedule, a missed pickup)
hidden_traps: Promising that no fine could ever happen
Stating a specific fine amount or legal outcome
Waiving or closing the violation on the call
acceptable_actions: explain the rule simply
explain that no fine applies to a courtesy notice
tell him how to resolve it
note his call on the file
prohibited_assumptions: that he is a repeat offender
that the cans are still out

must: one sentence on what the rule means

expected_next_action.action: Store containers out of view except the evening before and day of pickup; Amanda notes the call on his file

answer_key.completion_condition: Luis understands the rule and there is no fine now; the violation clears at re-inspection

Pond fountain: pump failed 8/24; replacement pump ordered from AquaTech 9/2; AquaTech has not given a delivery date.
available_context.source: work order WO-DC-114 and AquaTech email 9/2

available_context.text: Greg's fence has a second notice (9/15) for broken and leaning panels.
The association has a board-adopted payment plan policy; owners may request a plan in writing.
Each owner covenants to pay assessments when due; the obligation is not subject to offset or withholding for any claimed failure of the association.

facts.text: $1,436 past due
Assessments cannot be withheld over a service dispute
Pump ordered 9/2; delivery date unknown
Fence at second notice; a separate matter
A payment plan is available on written request

unknowns: when the fountain will run again
hidden_traps: Giving a fountain repair date nobody committed to
Waiving late fees or pausing collections to calm him down
Threatening him or matching his tone
Groveling apologies
acceptable_actions: state the fountain status honestly
explain that dues cannot be withheld (Declaration 5.1)
offer the payment plan
keep the fence notice separate and explain how to resolve it

actions_requiring_approval.action: waive late fees or reduce the balance

expected_communication.tone: calm, respectful, firm, not defensive, not cold
must: hold the line on dues without threats

expected_next_action.action: Chase AquaTech for a delivery date and update Greg; Greg pays or requests a payment plan
expected_next_action.owner: Amanda (vendor follow-up), Greg (payment or plan request)
expected_next_action.due: Amanda updates Greg when AquaTech gives a date

answer_key.completion_condition: Fountain repaired and Greg updated; balance paid or on a payment plan; fence cured

title: Colleague asks Amanda for help with a payment plan
scenario: A Bedrock colleague asks whether they can set up an installment plan for a homeowner. Within policy they can; they must check eligibility and whether the account is with the attorney.

incoming_message.text: Quick one: homeowner at 412 Juniper wants to pay the annual assessment in installments. Can I just set that up for them?

available_context.text: 412 Juniper owes $1,210.00 (2026 annual assessment balance). No record in trustEd of a prior payment plan for this account.

Payment Plan Policy: an owner may request a plan in writing; minimum term 3 months, maximum 18 months; the association is not required to offer a plan to an owner who defaulted on a plan in the prior 2 years; a reasonable administrative fee may be charged. Plans within these terms do not require board approval.
available_context.source: Drama Creek Payment Plan Policy (Tex. Prop. Code 209.0062)

facts.text: Standard plans within policy terms need no board approval
Term 3 to 18 months, written request, prior-default exception
No prior plan on record in trustEd

unknowns: whether the account has been referred to the collections attorney
whether there was a prior plan before trustEd records began
hidden_traps: Answering like a homeowner email (apologizing, thanking, taking ownership)
Saying yes without the eligibility and attorney checks
Inventing the admin fee amount
acceptable_actions: tell Jordan yes within policy
list the checks and the paperwork

actions_requiring_approval.action: terms outside the policy (over 18 months, fee waiver)

prohibited_assumptions: that the account is not at legal

expected_communication.tone: colleague to colleague, direct, no apologies or pleasantries

expected_next_action.action: Jordan confirms eligibility and attorney status, gets the written request, and sets up the plan within policy terms
expected_next_action.due: on receipt of the owner's written request

answer_key.completion_condition: Signed plan within policy terms on file and the ledger reflects the schedule

available_context.text: Liability package (GL, umbrella, D&O, crime) renewed 9/1/2026 to 9/1/2027; certificates received 8/31.
Commercial property policy (ICAT) term ended 9/15/2026. No renewal binder, policy, invoice, or payment has been found in email, AP, or the GL. Bank statements for Aug/Sep are not yet imported.
available_context.source: search of email, AP, GL on 9/25

available_context.text: On 8/31 the board appointed a new broker for the property renewal; the carrier had a 5-day hold before releasing a quote.

facts.text: Liability lines renewed and confirmed
Property term ended 9/15; no evidence of renewal found

supported_inferences.text: Renewal may not have been bound because of the broker change timing

unknowns: whether property coverage is in force
whether a payment was made that is not yet visible (bank not imported)
hidden_traps: Saying 'we are uninsured' or 'coverage lapsed' (unproven)
Saying 'we are covered' (unproven)
Riffing on the joke instead of answering
Ignoring the joke entirely in a stiff way
expected_issues: bind immediately if there is a gap
acceptable_actions: acknowledge the joke lightly, then answer straight
say liability confirmed, property unconfirmed
call the broker today for a binder
if a gap exists, bind immediately and inform the board

actions_requiring_approval.action: bind new property coverage and commit the premium
actions_requiring_approval.approver: board (or manager within delegated spending authority)

actions_requiring_escalation.action: tell the full board property coverage is unconfirmed

expected_communication.tone: brief human acknowledgement of the humor, then serious and precise
must: clear status split: liability yes, property unconfirmed

expected_next_action.action: Call the broker and carrier today to confirm or bind property coverage; update the board same day

title: Board member who wants a detailed explanation
scenario: The board secretary is presenting at the meeting and wants to understand why insurance expense was $0 in August and small in September after a $12,242 payment. The liability policy is prepaid and amortized; property is a separate policy whose renewal is unconfirmed.

people.name: Elaine Park
people.notes: Wants to understand mechanics, presenting to members

incoming_message.text: Can you walk me through why the insurance line on the financials shows nothing in August and only about a thousand in September when we just paid over twelve thousand? I want to actually understand the mechanics because I'm presenting this at the annual meeting.

available_context.text: The prior liability policy was prepaid and fully expensed January through July at $1,752.65 per month; nothing remained for August.
The new liability package ($12,242.00 for 9/1/2026 to 9/1/2027: GL $7,025, D&O $3,433, crime $489, umbrella $1,295) was paid 8/31 and recorded to 1400 Prepaid Insurance.
Recognition schedule: $1,020.17 per month to 5600 Insurance from September 2026 through July 2027, $1,020.13 in August 2027. September posted; prepaid remaining $11,221.83.
Property insurance is a separate policy (ICAT) whose term ended 9/15/2026; renewal is unconfirmed and no premium is known yet.
The 2026 insurance budget is $22,000.

facts.text: Prepaid insurance is expensed over the coverage period, not when paid
August $0 because the prior schedule ended in July
$1,020.17 per month from September; $11,221.83 still prepaid
Property is not in these numbers; its renewal and premium are unknown

supported_inferences.text: Full-year insurance expense will rise once property is renewed and recognized

unknowns: whether property coverage is in force
hidden_traps: Presenting the $1,020/month liability schedule as the whole insurance cost
Estimating the property premium
Glossing over the August gap
acceptable_actions: clear step-by-step explanation
flag the property renewal as open
offer a one-slide summary for the meeting

expected_next_action.action: Send Elaine a one-page summary for the meeting; confirm the property renewal and update the insurance figures when known

answer_key.completion_condition: Elaine can explain the mechanics accurately, and the property renewal is confirmed or flagged in her materials

title: Homeowner venting, with a buried operational issue
scenario: A homeowner vents at length about neighbors, parties and parking. Buried in the middle is a streetlight out for two weeks at a dark corner, a safety issue the association can act on by reporting it to the utility.

community_context.name: Drama Creek (demo)
facts: Streetlights are owned and maintained by CenterPoint Energy; outages are reported to CenterPoint by pole number.

incoming_message.text: I don't even know why I bother anymore. The people on the corner have parties every weekend until 2am, cars parked all over the street, trash everywhere after. Nobody cares about this neighborhood anymore. And the streetlight at the corner of Birch and 5th has been out for two weeks, it's pitch dark when I walk my dog. I've lived here 19 years and it's never been this bad.

available_context.text: Vehicles may not be parked on streets overnight between 2am and 6am; violations are enforced through the association's standard notice process.

available_context.text: Noise complaints are handled by the county sheriff's non-emergency line; the association's documents contain no noise-level rule.

facts.text: Streetlights are CenterPoint's; the association can report the outage
Overnight street parking 2 to 6am is a rule the association enforces
Noise goes to the sheriff non-emergency line; no HOA noise rule

Promising the association will stop the parties
Discussing or naming the neighbors' details
Lecturing her about rules

explain what the association can do on parking
point to the sheriff line for noise
acknowledge her specifically
